author: Raghu (Raghu.kuttan)
recording: Oriental scops owl calling; own field recording, December 2006, Parambikulam, Kerala, India
processing: Mono at 32 kHz; original excerpt; conservative spectral noise attenuation (45% subtraction, 55% floor) and 45 Hz rumble removal; linear gain to target -18 dBFS active level, peak cap -2 dBFS, 16 ms edge fades; original pitch and timing retained

commonName: Honey bees (species not identified by recorder)
author: kiwimana
recording: Honey bees returning to their hive, summer 2016; Waitakere Ranges, Auckland, New Zealand. Public high-quality MP3 preview of original field recording; species unspecified. Generic bee wing environment sound, not an Apis cerana call or an Asian recording.
processing: Mono at 32 kHz; original excerpt; DC removal only; linear gain to target -28 dBFS active level, peak cap -2 dBFS, 16 ms edge fades; original pitch and timing retained

author: Günter Tembrock; Museum für Naturkunde Berlin / Tierstimmenarchiv
recording: Three Asian black bears calling while being fed. Archive notes unspecified bird voices in the surrounding environment. Selected short low-frequency call excerpt; stationary hiss attenuated, no substitution of a different bear species.
processing: Mono 32 kHz native decoding; original excerpt; stationary noise attenuation using an adjacent source noise profile (85% subtraction, 20% floor); 45 Hz rumble removal; gain to -18 dBFS active-call target, gentle soft peak limiting only if needed with -2 dBFS ceiling; 18 ms edge fades; original pitch and timing retained
